claims.assertion: Swaruu defines shadow work as systematic introspection into learned programming, trauma, and automatic reactions.
claims.speaker: Swaruu

claims.assertion: She says social and family approval can repress disfavored traits and exaggerate accepted ones, forming conscious/unconscious divisions.
claims.speaker: Swaruu

claims.assertion: For Swaruu, a shadow is resisted behavior conflicting with self-concept; programming alone is not necessarily a shadow.
claims.speaker: Swaruu
claims.qualifiers: She says recognizing the resistance begins its resolution.

claims.assertion: She recommends identifying a troubling shadow, tracing its origins, choosing a response, then repeatedly building a positive association.
claims.speaker: Swaruu
claims.qualifiers: This is her approach; she rejects denial, not all negative attention.
